How does chaos gardening work?

Ecological gardening means seeing your garden as a living system. Soil, plants and insects work together.

A vegetable garden isn't nature. We intervene, harvest and adjust. That costs energy. The question is: how do we do that with nature, instead of against it?

Chaos gardening takes it a step further. Not with more control, but with better collaboration. You let plants combine, keep the soil covered, and use natural processes to your advantage.

Everything starts from three principles: close the loops, feed the soil, and work with diversity.

Interactive tools

Tools for the ecological gardener

Simple tools to better plan your garden — everything runs locally in your browser, no account or registration needed.

🌱

Mulch calculator

How much mulch does your garden need? Tell it the current state of your soil, what mulch material you have available, and what goal you're aiming for — the calculator shows how much mulch you'll need each year, and whether that's realistic with what you already have.

→ 🗺

Garden planner — paths, stepping stones & vegetables

First sketch your garden's layout: where the permanent paths go, where the beds go — the foundation of every ecological garden, so you never have to step on your soil. Then divide your vegetables across the beds: the tool takes accessibility into account and helps you pick combinations that strengthen each other.

The summary

10 commandments of the ecological gardener

1Above all, love your soil
2Keep it alive, don't let it spoil
3Compost feeds each seed you sow
4Stay on pathways where you go
5Ditch the chems and toxic pack
6On the mulch, do not hold back
7Shun the digging, shun the plough
8Plant and sow with pleasure now
9Mix your crops with clever care
10Most of all, enjoy and share!
